stem: Which statement correctly describes ribosomes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are made of DNA and protein, are found only in eukaryotic cells, and copy the genetic information of the nucleus.
choices.explanation: Ribosomes are made of rRNA and protein and are found in cells of all forms of life, including prokaryotes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are membrane-bound organelles made mostly of lipid, and they package finished proteins for transport out of the cell.
choices.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane and are not made of lipid. Packaging of proteins is a function of the Golgi complex.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are double-membrane organelles that contain their own DNA, and they make most of the ATP that the cell uses.
choices.explanation: This describes mitochondria. Ribosomes have no membrane and do not make ATP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are made of rRNA and protein, have no surrounding membrane, and make proteins from the sequence of messenger RNA.
choices.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane subcellular structures made of rRNA and protein. They synthesize proteins using the sequence of mRNA.

explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane structures of rRNA and protein that synthesize proteins from mRNA.

stem: Which observation about cells is best evidence that all known forms of life share a common ancestor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cells of all known forms of life contain mitochondria that make ATP by aerobic cellular respiration in the cell.
choices.explanation: Many prokaryotes have no mitochondria, so mitochondria are not found in all forms of life.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cells of all known forms of life contain chloroplasts that capture light energy and store it as chemical energy.
choices.explanation: Chloroplasts occur only in plants and photosynthetic algae, so they are not found in all forms of life.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cells of all known forms of life contain ribosomes that make proteins according to messenger RNA sequences.
choices.explanation: A structure found in the cells of every form of life is best explained by inheritance from a common ancestor.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cells of all known forms of life are surrounded by a cell wall that gives the cell its shape and its structure.
choices.explanation: Animal cells have no cell wall, so cell walls are not found in all forms of life.

explanation: Ribosomes occur in all forms of life, which reflects common ancestry.

stem: Which choice lists only structures that are part of the endomembrane system of a eukaryotic cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Golgi complex, chloroplasts, transport vesicles, the cell wall and the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Chloroplasts and the cell wall are not part of the endomembrane system.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, mitochondria, vacuoles and the nuclear envelope
choices.explanation: Ribosomes and mitochondria are not part of the endomembrane system.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, transport vesicles and the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: These membrane-bound structures work together to modify, package and transport proteins, lipids and polysaccharides.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ribosomes, mitochondria, chloroplasts, lysosomes, the Golgi complex and the cell wall
choices.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane, and mitochondria and chloroplasts are not part of the endomembrane system.

explanation: The endomembrane system includes the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, vacuoles and vesicles, the nuclear envelope and the plasma membrane.

stem: A gland cell makes large amounts of a protein that is secreted from the cell. Which structure is most likely to be abundant in this cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rough endoplasmic reticulum, which has ribosomes bound to its membrane and helps to carry out protein synthesis
choices.explanation: Rough ER is associated with membrane-bound ribosomes, and it helps with synthesizing proteins.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which has ribosomes bound to its membrane and makes most of the cell's proteins
choices.explanation: Smooth ER does not have bound ribosomes. It functions in lipid synthesis and detoxification.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lysosomes, which contain ribosomes in their interior and make proteins for the digestion of material in the cell
choices.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest material. They are not the site of protein synthesis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chloroplasts, which contain ribosomes on their outer membrane and make the proteins that are secreted from the cell
choices.explanation: Chloroplasts are the site of photosynthesis in plants and algae and are not in animal gland cells.

explanation: Rough ER has bound ribosomes and is involved in protein synthesis.

stem: Liver cells detoxify drugs and make lipids. Which organelle would be expected to be especially abundant in a liver cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chloroplasts, because they use light energy to break down drugs and to build lipids from carbon dioxide
choices.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plants and algae. They are not the site of detoxification in the liver.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The nuclear envelope, because it separates the cell's DNA from the toxins that are present in the cytoplasm
choices.explanation: The nuclear envelope encloses the nucleus. It does not detoxify drugs or make lipids.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, because its functions include detoxification and the synthesis of lipids
choices.explanation: Smooth ER is associated with detoxifying cells and with lipid synthesis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rough endoplasmic reticulum, because its bound ribosomes carry out detoxification and the synthesis of lipids
choices.explanation: Rough ER is associated with protein synthesis, not with detoxification and lipid synthesis.

explanation: Smooth ER functions in detoxification and in lipid synthesis.

stem: Which choice correctly describes functions of the Golgi complex?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It reads messenger RNA and joins amino acids into proteins, and then it packages the proteins into vesicles.
choices.explanation: Joining amino acids into proteins according to mRNA is the function of ribosomes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It chemically modifies and correctly folds newly made cellular products, and it packages proteins for trafficking.
choices.explanation: The Golgi complex is a series of flattened membrane sacs that modifies new products and packages proteins for transport.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It digests worn-out organelles with hydrolytic enzymes, and it releases the products into the cytoplasm for reuse.
choices.explanation: Digestion with hydrolytic enzymes is a function of lysosomes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes most of the ATP of the cell, and it also stores the proteins that it makes until they are needed.
choices.explanation: ATP is made mainly by mitochondria. The Golgi complex modifies and packages products.

explanation: The Golgi complex modifies, folds and packages cellular products.

stem: Mitochondria have a double membrane, and the inner membrane is highly folded. Which statement best explains how these features help the mitochondrion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The two membranes allow light energy to be captured, and the folds of the inner membrane store the glucose that is made there.
choices.explanation: Light is captured in chloroplasts. Mitochondria use energy stored in molecules to make ATP.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The two membranes provide separate compartments for different metabolic reactions, and the inner folds allow more efficient ATP synthesis.
choices.explanation: A double membrane provides compartments for reactions of aerobic respiration, and the folds increase the surface area for ATP synthesis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two membranes help the mitochondrion to make proteins, and the folds of the inner membrane carry the ribosomes.
choices.explanation: The main role of the folds is to increase the surface area for ATP synthesis, not to carry ribosomes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two membranes make a barrier that no molecules can cross, and the folds of the inner membrane keep the DNA protected inside the organelle.
choices.explanation: Molecules do cross the mitochondrial membranes through proteins. The folds increase membrane surface area.

explanation: The double membrane compartmentalizes respiration, and the folded inner membrane increases the surface area for making ATP.

stem: A white blood cell takes in a bacterium by forming a vesicle around it. Which organelle most likely fuses with this vesicle to digest the bacterium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A ribosome, which contains enzymes that break down the proteins of the bacterium into individual amino acids
choices.explanation: Ribosomes build proteins and do not digest material.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A chloroplast, which contains pigments that break down bacteria with light energy captured from the surroundings
choices.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plants and algae and capture light energy for photosynthesis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A large central vacuole, which is surrounded by water that dissolves the bacterium and stores the material
choices.explanation: A large central vacuole is a feature of plant cells and its main role is storage of nutrients and water.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A lysosome, which contains hydrolytic enzymes that digest material
choices.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-enclosed sacs of hydrolytic enzymes that digest material taken in by the cell.

explanation: Lysosomes digest material with hydrolytic enzymes.

stem: A houseplant wilts when it is not watered. Which structure of its cells is most directly involved in maintaining the turgor pressure that keeps the plant upright?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mitochondrion, which stores the water of the cell in the matrix and so keeps its cytoplasm full
choices.explanation: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration. They are not the main water store.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Golgi complex, which stores water in its flattened sacs and pumps it out to the cell wall as needed
choices.explanation: The Golgi complex modifies and packages products. It is not the main store of water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The large central vacuole, which stores water and nutrients and so maintains the turgor pressure of the cell
choices.explanation: In plant cells, a specialized large vacuole maintains turgor pressure through nutrient and water storage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The nucleus, which stores water in the nuclear envelope and releases it to the cytoplasm when the plant is dry
choices.explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA of the cell and is not the main store of water.

explanation: A large vacuole in plant cells maintains turgor pressure by storing water and nutrients.

stem: Which pair of organelles is surrounded by a double membrane?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transport vesicles and the rough ER
choices.explanation: Vesicles and the endoplasmic reticulum are bounded by a single membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lysosomes and vacuoles
choices.explanation: Lysosomes and vacuoles are surrounded by a single membrane.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts
choices.explanation: Both mitochondria and chloroplasts have a double membrane.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Golgi complex and ribosomes
choices.explanation: The Golgi complex has a single membrane, and ribosomes have no membrane.

explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have double membranes.

stem: The table shows the relative abundance of four structures in four types of cell. One of the cells makes and secretes large amounts of a protein hormone. Which cell is it most likely to be?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell 1, because it has a high abundance of rough ER, where proteins are made
choices.explanation: Rough ER has bound ribosomes that help with protein synthesis, which a protein-secreting cell needs in large amounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell 2, because it has a high abundance of smooth ER, where proteins are made
choices.explanation: Smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification, not with protein synthesis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cell 3, because it has a high abundance of mitochondria, where proteins are made
choices.explanation: Mitochondria make ATP. They are not the main site of protein synthesis for secretion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cell 4, because it has a high abundance of lysosomes, where proteins are made
choices.explanation: Lysosomes digest material and are not the site where proteins are made.

explanation: A cell that secretes a protein needs a lot of rough ER.

stem: A protein that will be secreted from a cell is made on a ribosome. Which sequence best describes the path of the protein through the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rough ER, transport vesicle, Golgi complex, secretory vesicle, plasma membrane
choices.explanation: The protein is made at the rough ER, moves in vesicles to the Golgi complex for modification, and is then packaged in vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nucleus, mitochondrion, rough ER, secretory vesicle, plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Proteins are not made in the nucleus and do not pass through the mitochondrion on the way out of the cell.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rough ER, lysosome, Golgi complex, nuclear envelope, plasma membrane
choices.explanation: A lysosome digests material and is not part of the secretion pathway, and the nuclear envelope is not on the path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Golgi complex, rough ER, lysosome, transport vesicle, nuclear envelope, plasma membrane
choices.explanation: The protein is made at the rough ER before it reaches the Golgi complex, and it is not taken to a lysosome for secretion.

explanation: Secreted proteins pass from rough ER to the Golgi complex in vesicles and then to the plasma membrane.

stem: Which of the following cells has the highest surface area-to-volume ratio?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A small cell, because its surface area is large compared with its volume
choices.explanation: A smaller cell has a higher surface area-to-volume ratio, so it can exchange materials efficiently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A cell of any size, because the surface area-to-volume ratio depends on the type of cell and not on its size
choices.explanation: The ratio depends on the size and shape of the cell. Smaller cells have higher ratios.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A large cell, because its large volume means that it has more membrane through which to exchange material
choices.explanation: Volume increases faster than surface area as a cell grows, so a large cell has a lower ratio.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cell with the most organelles, because its organelles increase the surface area of the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Organelles inside the cell do not change the surface area of the plasma membrane.

explanation: Smaller cells typically have a higher surface area-to-volume ratio.

stem: A cube-shaped cell has sides of length 3 µm. What is its surface area-to-volume ratio? (Surface area of a cube = 6s²; volume of a cube = s³.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 18 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: This divides the surface area by the side length (54 / 3). The ratio is the surface area divided by the volume.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2.0 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: Surface area = 6 x 3² = 54 µm² and volume = 3³ = 27 µm³, so the ratio is 54 / 27 = 2.0 per µm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 54 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: This is the surface area. The ratio is the surface area divided by the volume.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.5 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: This is the volume divided by the surface area, which is the inverse of the ratio that was asked for.

explanation: Surface area-to-volume ratio = surface area / volume = 6s² / s³ = 6 / s.

stem: A spherical cell has a radius of 5 µm. What is its surface area-to-volume ratio? (Surface area of a sphere = 4πr²; volume of a sphere = 4/3 πr³.)

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Surface area = 4π(5)² = 314 µm² and volume = 4/3 π(5)³ = 524 µm³, so the ratio is 314 / 524 = 0.60 per µm.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the ratio for a sphere with a radius of 10 µm (3 / 10). For a radius of 5 µm the ratio is 3 / 5 = 0.60.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1.7 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: This is the inverse of the ratio (524 / 314), the volume divided by the surface area.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 3.0 µm⁻¹
choices.explanation: This leaves out the division by the radius. For a sphere the ratio is 3 / r, which is 0.60 when r is 5 µm.

explanation: For a sphere the ratio simplifies to 3 / r.

stem: The radius of a spherical cell doubles as the cell grows. What happens to the surface area-to-volume ratio of the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It falls to one half of its original value, because volume increases eightfold and surface area fourfold.
choices.explanation: Doubling the radius multiplies the surface area by 2² = 4 and the volume by 2³ = 8, so the ratio is multiplied by 4 / 8 = 1/2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It decreases to one quarter of its original value, because the surface area of the cell increases fourfold.
choices.explanation: The volume increases eightfold as well, so the ratio falls to one half, not one quarter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It doubles, because the surface area and the volume both double when the radius of the cell doubles.
choices.explanation: Surface area increases fourfold and volume eightfold, not twofold.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It does not change, because the surface area and the volume of the cell increase by the same factor.
choices.explanation: Volume increases by a larger factor than surface area, so the ratio changes.

explanation: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area, so the ratio decreases.

stem: Which statement best explains why most cells are small?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a cell grows, its DNA is divided among more organelles, so the cell cannot make the proteins that it requires.
choices.explanation: This does not describe the limit set by the surface area-to-volume ratio.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a cell grows, its plasma membrane becomes thicker, so materials can no longer pass through it at all.
choices.explanation: The thickness of the membrane does not increase as a cell grows. The limit is the ratio of surface area to volume.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area, so the plasma membrane may not exchange materials fast enough for the cell.
choices.explanation: A decreasing surface area-to-volume ratio limits the exchange of nutrients and waste, which restricts cell size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As a cell grows, its surface area increases faster than its volume, so the cell has too much membrane for the amount of cytoplasm.
choices.explanation: The opposite is true: volume increases faster than surface area as a cell grows.

explanation: The surface area-to-volume ratio restricts cell size.

stem: The table shows the surface area and the volume of three cells. Which cell is best able to exchange materials with its environment, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell B, because it has a surface area that falls between the surface areas of the other two cells
choices.explanation: A value between the other two is not an advantage. The ratio of surface area to volume determines exchange.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell C, because it has the highest volume of the three cells and so holds the most materials
choices.explanation: A larger volume increases the demand for materials. What matters is the ratio of surface area to volume.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cell A, because it has the lowest surface area-to-volume ratio of the three cells
choices.explanation: A lower ratio means less surface for each unit of volume, which makes exchange less efficient.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cell C, because it has the highest surface area-to-volume ratio of the three cells
choices.explanation: The ratios are 0.75 for cell A, 1.5 for cell B and 2.0 for cell C. A higher ratio allows more efficient exchange.

explanation: A higher surface area-to-volume ratio allows more efficient exchange.

stem: Cells that line the small intestine have many tiny projections called microvilli on their surface. Which statement best explains how this feature helps the cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The projections increase the volume of the cell without changing its surface area, which allows more nutrients to be stored.
choices.explanation: Microvilli increase the surface area. Their effect on the volume is small.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The projections make the cell larger, which gives it a lower surface area-to-volume ratio and a faster rate of absorption.
choices.explanation: A lower ratio would make exchange less efficient. The projections raise the ratio.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The projections increase the surface area of the membrane without greatly increasing cell volume, which allows more absorption.
choices.explanation: Membrane folds and projections increase surface area, which improves the exchange of materials with the environment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The projections decrease the surface area of the plasma membrane, which keeps the nutrients inside the cell for longer.
choices.explanation: Projections increase the surface area. They do not decrease it.

explanation: More complex membrane structures, such as folds, allow more exchange with the environment.

stem: A shrew is a very small mammal and an elephant is a very large mammal. Which statement about the two animals is best supported by what is known about surface area-to-volume ratios?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The elephant loses heat to the environment faster for each gram of body mass and has a higher metabolic rate per unit of body mass.
choices.explanation: Larger organisms have a lower surface area-to-volume ratio, so they lose less heat for each gram of mass.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The shrew and the elephant lose heat at the same rate for each gram of body mass, because both are mammals.
choices.explanation: Heat loss for each gram of body mass depends on the surface area-to-volume ratio, which differs with size.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The shrew loses heat to the environment faster for each gram of body mass and has a higher metabolic rate per unit of body mass.
choices.explanation: Smaller organisms have a higher surface area-to-volume ratio, exchange more heat for their mass, and typically have a higher metabolic rate per unit of body mass.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The shrew loses heat to the environment more slowly for each gram of body mass and has a lower metabolic rate per unit of body mass.
choices.explanation: The shrew's higher surface area-to-volume ratio makes it lose heat faster, not more slowly.

explanation: Smaller organisms have higher surface area-to-volume ratios and higher metabolic rates per unit of mass.

stem: In a phospholipid bilayer, how are the phospholipid molecules arranged?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The phospholipids are arranged in a single layer with their hydrophilic heads pointing toward the cytoplasm and their tails toward the outside.
choices.explanation: The membrane is a double layer, and the heads of one layer face the outside of the cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All of the phospholipid molecules lie flat with their heads and tails mixed together in a single layer on the surface of the cell.
choices.explanation: A bilayer has two layers, with the tails of the two layers facing each other.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hydrophilic phosphate regions face the watery environments inside and outside the cell, and the fatty acid tails face each other in the interior.
choices.explanation: The polar heads are oriented toward the aqueous surroundings and the nonpolar tails are shielded from water in the middle of the bilayer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hydrophobic fatty acid tails face the watery environments inside and outside the cell, and the hydrophilic phosphate regions face each other.
choices.explanation: This reverses the arrangement. Hydrophobic tails face away from water.

explanation: Hydrophilic heads face the aqueous environments and hydrophobic tails face each other inside the membrane.

stem: Which statement best explains why phospholipids in water form a bilayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The polar phosphate heads are hydrophobic and cluster together away from water, while the nonpolar fatty acid tails interact with water.
choices.explanation: The phosphate heads are the hydrophilic part and the fatty acid tails are the hydrophobic part.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The phospholipids are attracted to the proteins in the membrane, and these proteins form a fixed frame that holds the layers in place.
choices.explanation: The bilayer forms because of the hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions of the phospholipids.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The nonpolar fatty acid tails are hydrophobic and cluster together away from water, while the polar phosphate heads interact with water.
choices.explanation: The two regions of a phospholipid behave differently in water, which produces the bilayer arrangement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The phospholipids are held together by covalent bonds that join the tails of one molecule to the heads of the next molecule.
choices.explanation: A bilayer is held together by weaker interactions. Phospholipids are not joined by covalent bonds to each other.

explanation: Phospholipids have both hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions, which determines their arrangement in water.

stem: Which regions of a protein embedded in a plasma membrane interact with the fatty acid tails in the interior of the membrane?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Regions made only of ionic side groups, which form strong bonds with the fatty acid tails in the interior of the membrane
choices.explanation: Ionic groups are hydrophilic and do not interact with the nonpolar tails.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Regions made of phosphate groups, which are covalently bonded to the fatty acid tails in the interior of the membrane
choices.explanation: Phosphate groups are part of the phospholipid heads and are not found in proteins in this way.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrophilic regions, which have charged and polar side groups and make up the surface of the protein within the membrane interior
choices.explanation: Hydrophilic regions are inside the protein or exposed to the cytosol, not in contact with the fatty acid tails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hydrophobic regions, which have nonpolar side groups and make up the surface of the protein within the membrane interior
choices.explanation: The hydrophobic regions of an embedded protein interact with the fatty acid tails of the phospholipids.

explanation: The hydrophobic regions of membrane proteins face the fatty acid tails.

stem: Which statement best describes the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The membrane is a framework of phospholipids embedded with proteins and other molecules that can move around within it.
choices.explanation: The model describes a flexible structure in which the components can move, like pieces in a mosaic that is fluid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The membrane is a single layer of phospholipids with a few proteins attached to the outside, which can move only along one axis.
choices.explanation: The membrane is a bilayer, with proteins embedded in it, and the components can move across its surface.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The membrane is a rigid sheet of protein that is coated with phospholipids, and none of its parts can move from place to place.
choices.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model, the phospholipids and proteins are not fixed in place.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The membrane is a layer of phospholipids that is surrounded on both sides by a continuous layer of protein that does not move.
choices.explanation: The proteins are embedded in the phospholipids, and the components can move.

explanation: In the fluid mosaic model the components of the membrane can move within it.

stem: Which choice lists components that are found in the plasma membranes of animal cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Phospholipids, proteins, cholesterol, glycoproteins and glycolipids
choices.explanation: Plasma membranes have a framework of phospholipids embedded with proteins, steroids such as cholesterol, glycoproteins and glycolipids.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phospholipids, proteins, starch, glycogen, cellulose and nucleotides
choices.explanation: Starch, glycogen and cellulose are polysaccharides that are not part of the plasma membrane.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proteins, DNA, cholesterol, glycoproteins and ribosomes
choices.explanation: DNA and ribosomes are not components of the plasma membrane.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Phospholipids, fatty acids, nucleotides, cellulose and glycolipids
choices.explanation: Nucleotides and cellulose are not components of the plasma membrane.

explanation: Plasma membranes contain phospholipids, proteins, cholesterol, glycoproteins and glycolipids.

stem: Researchers labeled the membrane proteins of two different cells with two different fluorescent dyes, fused the cells, and then measured the percent of cells in which the two dyes had mixed. The table shows the results at two temperatures. Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Membrane proteins are fixed in place in the plasma membrane, because the dyes mixed in only some of the cells after 10 minutes.
choices.explanation: The dyes mixed in all of the cells at 37 °C, which shows that proteins can move.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Membrane proteins move faster at the lower temperature, because the dyes mixed in fewer cells at 15 °C than they did at 37 °C.
choices.explanation: Fewer mixed cells at 15 °C means slower movement, not faster.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Membrane proteins move at the same rate at both temperatures, because the dyes eventually mixed in some of the cells at each temperature.
choices.explanation: The rates differ a great deal: 100 percent mixing at 37 °C after 40 minutes and 21 percent at 15 °C.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Membrane proteins can move within the plasma membrane, and they move more slowly at the lower temperature, consistent with the fluid mosaic model.
choices.explanation: The dyes mixed over time, so the proteins moved in the membrane. Mixing was much slower at 15 °C.

explanation: Mixing of the labels shows that membrane proteins move, and the temperature affects the fluidity of the membrane.

diagram.caption: Percent of fused cells in which the two dyes had mixed

stem: A mutation changes several nonpolar amino acids in the part of a membrane protein that lies within the membrane to polar amino acids. Which prediction is best supported by what is known about membrane proteins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The protein would move out of the membrane and into the cell wall, because polar amino acids are always found in cell walls.
choices.explanation: Animal cells have no cell wall, and polar amino acids are not limited to cell walls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The protein would be unchanged, because the amino acids inside the membrane do not affect how the protein is positioned.
choices.explanation: The properties of the amino acids determine how the protein interacts with its surroundings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The protein would be less likely to stay embedded, because the altered region would interact poorly with the nonpolar fatty acid tails.
choices.explanation: The region within the membrane is hydrophobic so that it can interact with the fatty acid tails. Polar amino acids there would interact poorly with the interior.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The protein would be more likely to stay embedded, because polar amino acids form stronger bonds with the fatty acid tails.
choices.explanation: Polar amino acids do not interact well with the nonpolar tails.

explanation: The hydrophobic regions of membrane proteins interact with the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.

stem: Which part of a phospholipid molecule is hydrophilic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The long fatty acid tails, which are made of chains of carbon and hydrogen atoms
choices.explanation: The fatty acid tails are nonpolar and hydrophobic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The polar phosphate region, which is oriented toward the watery environment
choices.explanation: The phosphate region of a phospholipid is polar and hydrophilic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The covalent bonds between the carbon atoms in each of the fatty acid tails
choices.explanation: These bonds are part of the hydrophobic tails.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The center of the bilayer, where the two layers of phospholipids meet each other
choices.explanation: The interior of the bilayer is hydrophobic.

explanation: The phosphate head of a phospholipid is hydrophilic; the fatty acid tails are hydrophobic.

stem: Which molecules can pass freely across the plasma membrane without the help of proteins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Large polar molecules, such as glucose, because they dissolve in water
choices.explanation: Large polar molecules need transport proteins to cross the membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small nonpolar molecules, such as oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
choices.explanation: Small nonpolar molecules freely pass across the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every molecule that is smaller than a protein, because the membrane is full of holes
choices.explanation: The bilayer has no holes. Its hydrophobic interior blocks many small molecules, such as ions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Charged ions, such as sodium and potassium ions, because they are small
choices.explanation: Ions are charged and cannot cross the hydrophobic interior without channel or transport proteins.

explanation: Small nonpolar molecules, such as N₂, O₂ and CO₂, pass freely through the membrane.

stem: Which molecules cross the plasma membrane through embedded channel proteins and transport proteins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the phospholipids that make up the membrane, as they move from one cell to another
choices.explanation: Phospholipids are a part of the membrane and are not transported across it by channel proteins.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrophilic substances, such as ions and large polar molecules
choices.explanation: Hydrophilic substances cannot cross the hydrophobic interior directly, so they move through channels and transport proteins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the fatty acids that make up the tails of the phospholipids in the bilayer
choices.explanation: Fatty acids are a part of the membrane lipids. They are not moved by channel proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Small nonpolar molecules, such as oxygen and carbon dioxide
choices.explanation: These pass freely through the membrane without help.

explanation: Ions and large polar molecules need channels and transport proteins.

stem: Which statement best explains why ions such as Na⁺ cannot pass directly through the lipid bilayer of the plasma membrane?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ions are too large to fit between the phospholipids, which are packed tightly with no spaces between the heads.
choices.explanation: The barrier is not size alone. The charged ions are blocked by the nonpolar interior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cell makes enzymes that break down all ions at the surface of the membrane before they have a chance to enter.
choices.explanation: Ions are not broken down by enzymes at the membrane. They are blocked by the hydrophobic interior.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The nonpolar hydrocarbon tails in the interior of the membrane prevent charged particles and polar molecules from crossing.
choices.explanation: The hydrophobic interior is the barrier that makes the membrane selectively permeable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The polar phosphate heads of the phospholipids attract ions so strongly that they hold them at the surface of the membrane.
choices.explanation: Heads on the surface can interact with ions, but the main barrier is the hydrophobic interior.

explanation: The nonpolar hydrocarbon tails prevent ions and polar molecules from crossing the membrane.

stem: The table shows how quickly different substances cross an artificial lipid bilayer that contains no proteins, in arbitrary units. Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water cannot cross the bilayer at all, because the rate for water is lower than the rates for the gases in the table.
choices.explanation: The rate for water is not zero. A small amount of water crosses the bilayer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Small nonpolar molecules cross the bilayer more slowly than polar molecules and ions, because they are repelled by the hydrophilic heads.
choices.explanation: The data show the opposite: oxygen and carbon dioxide have the highest values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All of the substances cross the bilayer at about the same rate, because the bilayer does not have any selective properties.
choices.explanation: The rates range from 100 to 0.001, so the bilayer discriminates among substances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Small nonpolar molecules cross the bilayer much faster than polar molecules and ions, consistent with the hydrophobic interior.
choices.explanation: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross fastest. Water crosses slowly, and glucose and sodium ions cross very slowly.

explanation: A bilayer is selectively permeable, with small nonpolar molecules crossing most easily.
