diagram.caption: Crossing an artificial bilayer

stem: Bacteria, archaea, fungi and plants all have cell walls. Which statement describes a role of the cell wall?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It stores the genetic information of the cell, because the cell wall contains the DNA in a protected compartment.
choices.explanation: DNA is not stored in the cell wall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It provides the energy that the cell needs, because the cell wall is where the ATP of the cell is made.
choices.explanation: ATP is made in mitochondria or across the plasma membrane. It is not made in the cell wall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It makes the plasma membrane selectively permeable, because the cell wall has a hydrophobic interior that blocks ions.
choices.explanation: The hydrophobic interior of the plasma membrane makes it selectively permeable. The cell wall does not do this.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It provides a structural boundary and a permeability barrier, and it protects the cell from bursting when water enters.
choices.explanation: Cell walls give structure, act as a barrier for some substances, and protect cells from osmotic lysis.

explanation: Cell walls provide a structural boundary, a permeability barrier and protection from osmotic lysis.

stem: A bacterium whose cell wall has been removed bursts when it is placed in pure water, but a bacterium with an intact cell wall does not. Which statement best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cell wall gives structure and protects the cell from osmotic lysis, so the intact cell resists the water that enters.
choices.explanation: Water enters the cell by osmosis, and the cell wall prevents the cell from swelling until it bursts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cell wall makes the plasma membrane thicker, so the intact bacterium loses water by osmosis instead of gaining it.
choices.explanation: The cell wall does not thicken the plasma membrane, and water moves into the cell in pure water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cell wall provides the cell with an extra supply of ATP, so the intact bacterium can pump out all of the water.
choices.explanation: The cell wall does not supply ATP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cell wall keeps water out of the cell completely, so no water can enter the intact bacterium in pure water.
choices.explanation: Water can cross the cell wall and enter. The wall resists the swelling and bursting of the cell.

explanation: The cell wall protects against osmotic lysis.

stem: A researcher hypothesizes that the hydrophobic interior of the membrane prevents the movement of sodium ions unless a channel protein is present. Which result would best support this hypothesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An artificial bilayer with channel proteins is less permeable to sodium ions than a bilayer without proteins, since proteins block the ions.
choices.explanation: This would contradict the hypothesis that the channel proteins allow ions through.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An artificial bilayer without proteins is almost impermeable to sodium ions, but the permeability increases greatly when channel proteins for sodium are added.
choices.explanation: This result shows that the lipid bilayer alone blocks the ions and that the channel proteins allow them across.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An artificial bilayer without proteins is permeable to sodium ions only when the temperature is raised, and channel proteins make no difference.
choices.explanation: This does not test the role of the interior or of the proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An artificial bilayer without proteins is highly permeable to sodium ions, and adding channel proteins for sodium has no effect on its permeability.
choices.explanation: This would show that the bilayer does not block the ions.

explanation: Evidence for a hypothesis comes from a comparison in which only the factor being tested is changed.

stem: Water is a polar molecule, yet a small amount of water crosses the lipid bilayer of a plasma membrane without the help of any protein. Which statement best explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water is a charged ion that is attracted to the phosphate heads, so it is carried through the interior of the membrane by the heads.
choices.explanation: Water molecules are not charged, and the interior of the membrane is not crossed by being carried by the heads.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Water is too large to enter any channel, so the only way it can cross the membrane is by active transport using energy from ATP.
choices.explanation: Water can cross by passive transport, and aquaporins can carry water in large quantities without direct input of energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Water is a small polar molecule with no charge, and small polar uncharged molecules can pass through the membrane in small amounts.
choices.explanation: Small, uncharged polar molecules, such as water and ammonia, can slip through the bilayer, although only in small amounts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water is a nonpolar molecule when it is in contact with a membrane, so it passes through the hydrophobic interior as easily as oxygen does.
choices.explanation: Water remains polar. It crosses the bilayer far more slowly than small nonpolar molecules do.

explanation: Small polar uncharged molecules, such as H₂O and NH₃, cross the membrane in small amounts.

stem: Which statement correctly describes passive transport?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the movement of molecules in which each molecule must be moved by a protein that is powered directly by the hydrolysis of ATP.
choices.explanation: Passive transport does not directly use the energy of ATP.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the movement of large particles into the cell by the folding of the plasma membrane to make a vesicle around them.
choices.explanation: This describes endocytosis, which requires energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the net movement of molecules from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration using energy from ATP.
choices.explanation: This describes active transport.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the net movement of molecules from a region of high concentration to one of low concentration without direct input of energy.
choices.explanation: Passive transport moves molecules down their concentration gradient and does not need direct input of energy.

explanation: Passive transport is movement down a concentration gradient with no direct input of metabolic energy.

stem: Which statement correctly describes active transport?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It requires a direct input of energy and always moves molecules from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
choices.explanation: Active transport can move molecules against a gradient, from low to high concentration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It requires a direct input of energy and, in some cases, moves molecules from low concentration to high concentration.
choices.explanation: Active transport uses energy to move molecules, including against their concentration gradients.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It requires no input of energy and moves molecules only through the phospholipid bilayer and never through proteins.
choices.explanation: Active transport requires energy and it needs membrane proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires no input of energy and always moves molecules from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration.
choices.explanation: Active transport requires energy, and the direction is not always against the gradient in this way.

explanation: Active transport requires a direct input of energy.

stem: Which feature of the plasma membrane allows concentration gradients of solutes to form across it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The membrane is completely permeable, so every substance crosses it at the same rate in both directions.
choices.explanation: If the membrane were completely permeable, gradients could not be maintained.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The membrane is made of a single type of protein, so all of the substances cross it through the same channel.
choices.explanation: The membrane has a phospholipid bilayer with different proteins in it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The membrane is completely impermeable, so no substances are able to cross it in either direction at any time.
choices.explanation: A membrane that nothing could cross would not allow the cell to take in nutrients.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The membrane is selectively permeable, so some substances cross it more easily than others.
choices.explanation: Selective permeability allows different concentrations of solutes to be established on the two sides of the membrane.

explanation: Selective permeability allows concentration gradients to form.

stem: Which statement correctly describes endocytosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cell releases large molecules by fusing vesicles with the plasma membrane so that their contents are secreted to the outside.
choices.explanation: This describes exocytosis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cell takes in large molecules or particles by folding the plasma membrane in on itself and forming vesicles that engulf the material.
choices.explanation: In endocytosis, new small vesicles form from the plasma membrane and enclose material from outside the cell.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cell takes in ions by opening channel proteins so that the ions can move down their concentration gradient.
choices.explanation: This describes facilitated diffusion through channel proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cell takes in small nonpolar molecules by letting them pass directly through the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.
choices.explanation: Small nonpolar molecules move directly across the membrane by passive transport, and this is not endocytosis.

explanation: Endocytosis takes material into the cell in vesicles formed from the plasma membrane.

stem: Cells of the pancreas release the protein hormone insulin into the blood. Which process moves this large molecule out of the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Facilitated diffusion, in which the insulin moves down its gradient through a channel protein in the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Large molecules such as proteins are too large to pass through channel proteins.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exocytosis, in which vesicles that contain the insulin fuse with the plasma membrane and release their contents
choices.explanation: Exocytosis secretes large molecules by fusion of vesicles with the plasma membrane. It requires energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Passive diffusion, in which the insulin passes directly through the hydrophobic interior of the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Insulin is a large molecule that cannot cross the hydrophobic interior of the membrane by itself.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endocytosis, in which the plasma membrane folds in and forms vesicles that carry the insulin out of the cell
choices.explanation: Endocytosis takes material into the cell.

explanation: Exocytosis moves large molecules out of the cell.

stem: A researcher measures the concentration of three substances inside and outside a cell and determines the direction of the net movement of each substance across the plasma membrane, as shown in the table. Which substance is most likely moved by active transport?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Substance R, because it moves from the lower concentration outside the cell to the higher concentration inside the cell
choices.explanation: Net movement against the concentration gradient requires a direct input of energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Substance P, because it moves from the higher concentration inside the cell to the lower concentration outside the cell
choices.explanation: This is also movement down the concentration gradient, which is consistent with passive transport.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Substance Q, because it moves from the higher concentration outside the cell to the lower concentration inside the cell
choices.explanation: This is movement down the concentration gradient, which is consistent with passive transport.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None of the substances, because the concentrations differ across the membrane for all three substances in the table
choices.explanation: A concentration difference is expected across the membrane and does not rule out active transport.

explanation: Active transport can move a substance against its concentration gradient.

stem: Which of the following processes require a direct input of metabolic energy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The diffusion of oxygen, the diffusion of carbon dioxide and exocytosis
choices.explanation: Diffusion of gases is passive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Active transport across the membrane, endocytosis and exocytosis
choices.explanation: Active transport, endocytosis and exocytosis require energy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Facilitated diffusion, osmosis and endocytosis
choices.explanation: Facilitated diffusion and osmosis are passive. Only endocytosis in this list requires energy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osmosis, the diffusion of oxygen and the movement of ions through channels
choices.explanation: All three of these are passive and need no direct input of energy.

explanation: Active transport, endocytosis and exocytosis require energy.

stem: A researcher wants to test whether a molecule enters cells by active transport. Which investigation would best test this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Measure the uptake of the molecule by two different samples of cells without any treatment, and see whether the uptake is the same.
choices.explanation: Without changing the supply of energy, this cannot show whether the uptake needs energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measure the uptake of the molecule by cells with and without a chemical that stops ATP production, and see whether uptake against the gradient falls.
choices.explanation: If the uptake against the gradient depends on energy, a metabolic inhibitor will reduce it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measure the uptake of the molecule by cells in solutions with different concentrations of salt, and see whether the cells change in size.
choices.explanation: This tests the effects of osmosis on cells, not the role of energy in the movement of the molecule.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measure the size of the molecule with a microscope, and see whether it is smaller than the largest channel in the membrane.
choices.explanation: The size of the molecule does not show whether it is moved by active transport.

explanation: To test whether transport needs energy, compare uptake with and without a block on energy supply.

stem: Which statement correctly describes facilitated diffusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Channel proteins or transport proteins allow substances to move down their concentration gradient across the membrane without an input of energy.
choices.explanation: Facilitated diffusion is passive transport that needs membrane proteins but does not use energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The plasma membrane folds in and forms vesicles that take large particles into the cell, using energy that is supplied by the cell.
choices.explanation: This describes endocytosis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Substances pass directly through the hydrophobic interior of the phospholipid bilayer, without the help of any protein, down their gradient.
choices.explanation: This describes simple diffusion. Facilitated diffusion needs proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transport proteins use energy from ATP to move substances from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration across the membrane.
choices.explanation: This describes active transport, which needs energy.

explanation: Facilitated diffusion uses channel or transport proteins and needs no energy.

stem: Sodium ions and potassium ions need channel proteins to cross the plasma membrane. Which statement best explains why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ions are nonpolar, so they are repelled by the polar heads of the phospholipids on both sides of the membrane.
choices.explanation: Ions are charged and polar interactions are not what block them. The hydrophobic interior blocks them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ions are charged, so they cannot pass through the hydrophobic interior of the lipid bilayer without a channel.
choices.explanation: Charged ions are blocked by the nonpolar interior of the membrane and cross through channel proteins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ions are too large to pass between the phospholipid molecules, which are packed too tightly for the ions to fit.
choices.explanation: The barrier is the charge of the ions and the hydrophobic interior, not only the size of the ions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ions are produced inside the membrane by proteins, so they must be moved out through channels to the cytoplasm.
choices.explanation: Ions are not made inside the membrane. They come from the solutions on either side.

explanation: Charged ions require channel proteins to cross the membrane.

stem: Glucose is a large polar molecule. Cells take glucose in from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, without using any ATP, through a protein in the membrane. Which process is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exocytosis, which moves large polar molecules out of the cell inside vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane using energy
choices.explanation: In this case the molecule moves into the cell without using energy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Facilitated diffusion, which moves large polar molecules through membranes down a concentration gradient with no energy input
choices.explanation: Large polar molecules move through transport proteins down the gradient in facilitated diffusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Active transport, which moves large polar molecules through membranes down a concentration gradient using energy from ATP
choices.explanation: No ATP is used in this process, so it is not active transport.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Simple diffusion, which moves large polar molecules directly through the lipid bilayer down a concentration gradient with no protein
choices.explanation: A protein is involved in this process, and large polar molecules do not cross the bilayer directly.

explanation: Facilitated diffusion enables large polar molecules to move down their gradient through a protein with no energy input.

stem: The cells of the kidney move large quantities of water across their membranes. Which membrane proteins make this rapid movement of water possible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycoproteins, which bind water molecules on the outside of the cell and carry them into the cytoplasm
choices.explanation: Glycoproteins are involved in other functions. Aquaporins transport the water.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phospholipids, which form a pore in the bilayer that lets water pass through in large quantities
choices.explanation: Phospholipids form a barrier, and only a small amount of water crosses the bilayer directly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aquaporins, which transport large quantities of water across the membrane
choices.explanation: Aquaporins are channel proteins that allow large amounts of water to cross membranes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sodium-potassium pumps, which use ATP to carry water across the membrane against its concentration gradient
choices.explanation: These pumps move Na⁺ and K⁺, and water moves by osmosis.

explanation: Aquaporins transport large quantities of water across membranes.

stem: The graph shows the rate at which cells take up two molecules, X and Y, at different external concentrations. Which statement best explains why the rate of uptake of molecule Y levels off at high concentrations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The transport proteins that move molecule Y become saturated, so a higher concentration cannot increase the rate.
choices.explanation: A limited number of transport proteins can only carry molecules at a maximum rate, which leads to a plateau.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The membrane runs out of phospholipids at high concentrations, so no more of molecule Y can cross the bilayer.
choices.explanation: The number of phospholipids does not limit the rate. The number of transport proteins does.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cell uses up its ATP at high concentrations, so it can no longer move molecule Y in the direction of the gradient.
choices.explanation: Facilitated diffusion does not use ATP, and the plateau is explained by the limited number of proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The molecules of Y are denatured at high concentrations, so they can no longer pass through channels in the membrane.
choices.explanation: A plateau in the rate does not indicate that the molecules are denatured. It shows that the proteins are saturated.

explanation: Facilitated diffusion has a maximum rate, because the number of transport proteins is limited.

diagram.altText: Rate of uptake against external concentration. For molecule X the rate rises in a straight line from 0 to 40. For molecule Y the rate rises steeply to about 32 at 20 millimolar and then levels off near 36.

stem: Based on the graph, which statement about how molecules X and Y cross the membrane is best supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Molecule X probably crosses by facilitated diffusion, since its rate increases steadily, and molecule Y probably crosses by simple diffusion, since its rate reaches a maximum.
choices.explanation: This reverses the interpretation. A maximum rate suggests that proteins are involved.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both molecules probably cross by simple diffusion, since the rates for both of them are above zero at every concentration shown.
choices.explanation: The two graphs differ in shape, and the plateau for molecule Y is not expected for simple diffusion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Molecule X probably crosses by simple diffusion, since its rate increases steadily, and molecule Y probably crosses by facilitated diffusion, since its rate reaches a maximum.
choices.explanation: A rate that keeps increasing with concentration fits simple diffusion, and a rate that reaches a maximum fits a process that depends on a limited number of proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both molecules probably cross by active transport, since the rates for both of them are higher at higher external concentrations.
choices.explanation: A higher rate at a higher concentration does not show that energy is used.

explanation: Saturation at high concentration indicates facilitated diffusion.

diagram.altText: Rate of uptake against external concentration. For molecule X the rate rises in a straight line from 0 to 40. For molecule Y the rate rises steeply to about 32 at 20 millimolar and then levels off near 36.

stem: A mutation reduces the number of potassium channel proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction is most consistent with this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The movement of water across the membrane would stop, since potassium channels are the only proteins that water can cross through.
choices.explanation: Water moves through the bilayer and through aquaporins, not through potassium channels.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The movement of potassium ions across the membrane would be slower, since the ions need channel proteins to cross the membrane.
choices.explanation: Potassium ions are charged and need channels. Fewer channels means a lower rate of movement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The movement of potassium ions across the membrane would be faster, since the ions have fewer channels that they need to pass through.
choices.explanation: Fewer channels would slow the movement, not speed it up.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The movement of potassium ions across the membrane would not change, since the ions can pass directly through the lipid bilayer.
choices.explanation: Charged ions cannot pass directly through the hydrophobic interior of the bilayer.

explanation: Ions such as K⁺ require channel proteins for facilitated diffusion.

stem: The movement of sodium ions and potassium ions through channel proteins can change the electrical charge difference across a membrane. Which statement best explains why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ions are changed into neutral molecules as they cross the membrane, so a charge difference builds up on one side.
choices.explanation: The ions stay charged as they cross. The movement of charge is what changes the difference.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ions carry electrical charge, so their net movement changes how the charge is distributed on the two sides of the membrane.
choices.explanation: The membrane can become polarized by the movement of charged ions across it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The channel proteins are made of metal, so they conduct electrical current in the same way that a wire conducts it.
choices.explanation: Channel proteins are not metal. They are made of amino acids.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ions are nonpolar, so they bring an electrical charge with them only when they combine with the phospholipids of the bilayer.
choices.explanation: Ions are charged, and the charge does not depend on combining with phospholipids.

explanation: Membranes may become polarized by the movement of ions across them.

stem: A red blood cell is placed in a solution that has a higher concentration of solutes than the cytoplasm of the cell. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The solution is hypertonic to the cell, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis and the cell shrinks.
choices.explanation: In a hypertonic solution the water potential is lower outside, so water leaves the cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The solution is hypotonic to the cell, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis and the cell shrinks.
choices.explanation: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration, and water would move into the cell.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The solution is isotonic to the cell, so water moves out of the cell by osmosis until the cell is completely empty.
choices.explanation: An isotonic solution has the same solute concentration, and there is no net movement of water.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The solution is hypertonic to the cell, so water moves into the cell by osmosis and the cell swells and bursts.
choices.explanation: Water moves toward the higher solute concentration, which is outside, so the cell loses water.

explanation: Water moves from the hypotonic to the hypertonic side.

stem: Solution A has a water potential of -2.0 bars and solution B has a water potential of -5.0 bars. The two solutions are separated by a membrane that is permeable to water but not to solutes. What is the net movement of water?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From solution B to solution A, because water moves toward the region that has the lower solute concentration
choices.explanation: Water moves toward the lower water potential, which is the more negative value of solution B.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is no net movement, because the membrane does not allow any solutes to cross from one solution to the other
choices.explanation: The difference in water potential drives the movement of water across the membrane.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From solution A to solution B, because solution A has the higher water potential
choices.explanation: Water moves by osmosis from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential. -2.0 is higher than -5.0.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From solution B to solution A, because solution B has the larger number of the two values when the signs are ignored
choices.explanation: Water potential is compared with the sign, and -5.0 is lower than -2.0.

explanation: Water moves from high water potential to low water potential.

stem: A plant cell and an animal cell are each placed in distilled water. Which outcome is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both cells shrink because water moves out of them into the distilled water, which has more water than the cells.
choices.explanation: Distilled water is hypotonic to both cells, so water moves into them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The plant cell bursts because its cell wall breaks, and the animal cell becomes firm because it has no wall.
choices.explanation: The cell wall protects plant cells from lysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The plant cell becomes firm (turgid) because its cell wall resists the water that enters, and the animal cell may burst.
choices.explanation: Water enters both cells by osmosis. The wall of the plant cell protects it from lysis, but the animal cell has no wall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both cells stay the same size because the distilled water is isotonic to the cytoplasm of both of the cells.
choices.explanation: Distilled water contains no solutes, so it is hypotonic to the cells.

explanation: A cell wall protects plant cells from osmotic lysis in hypotonic solutions.

stem: What is the solute potential of a 0.20 M sucrose solution at 27 °C? (Ψₛ = -iCRT, where i = 1.0 for sucrose, and R = 0.0831 L bar / mol K.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: -4.99 bars

choices.label: B
choices.text: -0.45 bars
choices.explanation: This uses the temperature in degrees Celsius (27) instead of kelvin (300).

choices.label: C
choices.text: +4.99 bars
choices.explanation: The solute potential of a solution is negative. The equation has a minus sign.

choices.label: D
choices.text: -9.97 bars
choices.explanation: This uses i = 2, which is the ionization constant for a substance that separates into two ions, such as sodium chloride. Sucrose does not ionize, so i = 1.

explanation: Solute potential = -iCRT, with the temperature in kelvin.

stem: A plant cell has a pressure potential of +2.0 bars and a solute potential of -6.5 bars. It is placed in an open beaker that contains a solution with a solute potential of -4.0 bars. In which direction is there a net movement of water?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There is no net movement, because the pressure potential of the cell balances out the solute potential of the cell
choices.explanation: The cell has a total water potential of -4.5 bars, not zero, and it differs from the solution.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Out of the cell, because the water potential of the cell, -4.5 bars, is higher than the water potential of the solution, -4.0 bars
choices.explanation: -4.5 is lower than -4.0, so the cell has the lower water potential and water moves into it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Into the cell, because the solution has a water potential of -4.0 bars, which is higher than that of the cell (-4.5 bars)
choices.explanation: Water potential = pressure potential + solute potential. The cell is at +2.0 + (-6.5) = -4.5 bars and the solution (pressure potential of zero in an open beaker) is at -4.0 bars.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Out of the cell, because the positive pressure potential of +2.0 bars pushes water out through the plasma membrane
choices.explanation: Pressure potential is part of the water potential of the cell, and the total is -4.5 bars, which is lower than that of the solution.

explanation: Water moves from the higher total water potential to the lower one.

stem: Potato cores of the same initial mass were placed in sucrose solutions of different concentrations for 24 hours, and the percent change in mass of each core was measured, as shown in the table. Which concentration of sucrose is closest to the solute concentration inside the cells of the potato?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 0.50 M, the concentration that is halfway between the two concentrations at which the mass changed from a gain to a loss
choices.explanation: The point of no change is closer to 0.4 M, since the gain at 0.4 M (+1.0) is much smaller than the loss at 0.6 M (-8.0).

choices.label: B
choices.text: 0.40 M, the concentration of the tested solution at which the percent change in mass has the smallest absolute value
choices.explanation: This is the nearest tested value, but the line through the data crosses zero a little above 0.4 M, at about 0.42 M.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 0.00 M, the concentration at which the potato cores had the largest change in mass because of the water they took up
choices.explanation: At 0.0 M the cores gained the most water, so that solution was the most hypotonic to the cells.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.42 M, the concentration at which a straight line through the data points for 0.4 M and 0.6 M shows no change in mass
choices.explanation: The cores neither gained nor lost mass when the solution was isotonic to the cells. Between 0.4 M (+1.0 percent) and 0.6 M (-8.0 percent), the change in mass is zero at about 0.42 M.

explanation: The solution that is isotonic to the cells is the one in which the mass does not change; interpolate between the data points.

stem: Freshwater protists that live in ponds have a structure called a contractile vacuole. Which statement best explains why they need it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cytoplasm and the pond water are isotonic, so the vacuole is needed to move water against a gradient that does not exist.
choices.explanation: In an isotonic solution no net movement of water occurs, and no vacuole would be needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cytoplasm of the protist is hypertonic to the pond water, so water enters by osmosis and the contractile vacuole pumps the excess out.
choices.explanation: Osmoregulation lets organisms control their water balance. In fresh water, water moves into the cell by osmosis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pond water is hypertonic to the cytoplasm, so water leaves the cell by osmosis and the vacuole stores the extra water.
choices.explanation: Pond water is dilute, so it is hypotonic to the cytoplasm and water enters the cell.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cytoplasm of the protist is hypotonic to the pond water, so water enters by osmosis and the vacuole pumps the water out.
choices.explanation: If the cytoplasm were hypotonic to the pond water, water would move out of the cell.

explanation: A contractile vacuole removes the water that enters a freshwater protist by osmosis.

stem: A plant cell is placed in a solution that is hypertonic to the cell. Which description of the cell is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water leaves the cell, the plasma membrane presses against the cell wall, and the pressure potential of the cell increases.
choices.explanation: A cell that loses water loses pressure and does not press against the wall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is no net movement of water, the plasma membrane stays in contact with the cell wall, and the cell stays the same.
choices.explanation: A hypertonic solution causes a net loss of water from the cell.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Water enters the cell, the plasma membrane presses against the cell wall, and the pressure potential of the cell increases.
choices.explanation: This describes a plant cell in a hypotonic solution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water leaves the cell, the plasma membrane pulls away from the cell wall, and the pressure potential of the cell decreases.
choices.explanation: Water leaves a plant cell in a hypertonic solution, so the cell loses turgor pressure and the membrane shrinks away from the wall.

explanation: In a hypertonic solution a plant cell loses water and turgor pressure.

stem: A cell is placed in a solution that is isotonic to its cytoplasm. Which statement about the movement of water is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water molecules move across the membrane in both directions at equal rates, so there is no net movement of water.
choices.explanation: In an isotonic solution the water potentials are equal, so water moves into and out of the cell at the same rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Water molecules move only out of the cell, because the solution has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm has.
choices.explanation: In an isotonic solution the water potentials are the same.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Water molecules do not cross the membrane at all, because the solute concentrations on both sides of it are equal.
choices.explanation: Water molecules still move across the membrane. There is no net movement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water molecules move only into the cell, because the cell has a larger number of solutes than the solution has.
choices.explanation: The solute concentrations are equal in an isotonic solution.

explanation: In an isotonic solution there is no net movement of water.

stem: The graph shows the mean percent change in mass of beet cores after 24 hours in three sucrose solutions. Each mean is from six cores, and the error bars show plus and minus 2 standard errors of the mean. Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cores lost mass in all three solutions, because the 0.6 M solution has the largest error bar of the three.
choices.explanation: Only the 0.6 M solution shows a loss of mass. The size of an error bar does not tell the direction of a change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The mean change in mass differs among the three solutions, because none of the error bars overlap, and the cores lost mass in the 0.6 M solution.
choices.explanation: Because the error bars do not overlap, the differences between the means are unlikely to be due to chance. The negative value means a loss of mass.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cores took up water in the 0.6 M solution, because the solution contains the largest amount of dissolved sucrose.
choices.explanation: The 0.6 M solution is hypertonic to the cells, so the cores lost water and mass.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mean change in mass is not different between the 0.0 M and 0.3 M solutions, because both of the means are above zero and so must be the same.
choices.explanation: Both means are above zero, but the error bars do not overlap, so the two means differ.

explanation: Error bars that do not overlap suggest real differences between the means.

stem: A plant cell that is turgid in distilled water is moved to a 0.5 M sucrose solution. Which prediction is best supported by what is known about osmosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Water will not move, because the cell wall prevents water from crossing in either direction.
choices.explanation: The cell wall does not stop water crossing. It resists the swelling of the cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Water will leave the cell by osmosis, and the pressure potential of the cell will increase.
choices.explanation: A cell that loses water loses pressure, not gains it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Water will enter the cell by osmosis, and the pressure potential of the cell will increase.
choices.explanation: Water enters when the solution is hypotonic, and this solution is hypertonic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Water will leave the cell by osmosis, and the pressure potential of the cell will decrease.
choices.explanation: The solution has a lower water potential than the cell, so water leaves and the cell loses turgor pressure.

explanation: Moving a plant cell to a hypertonic solution makes it lose water and turgor.

stem: Which statement best describes osmoregulation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is the set of mechanisms that organisms use to control their water balance and their internal solute concentration.
choices.explanation: Osmoregulation maintains water balance and lets organisms control their internal solute composition and water potential.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the production of new cells to replace those that have burst, which keeps the total volume of an organism constant.
choices.explanation: Osmoregulation controls water and solutes in cells. It is not the replacement of cells.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the movement of solutes into a cell by active transport, which is the only way that water balance can be controlled.
choices.explanation: Osmoregulation involves control of water and solutes, and active transport is not the only mechanism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the movement of water out of a cell by osmosis until the solute concentration in the cell is the same as it is outside.
choices.explanation: Osmoregulation is the control of water balance and does not just mean water leaving a cell until the concentrations are equal.

explanation: Osmoregulation maintains water balance and control of solute composition.

stem: What is needed to move ions across a membrane by active transport?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cell wall only, because the wall pushes the ions across the membrane by applying pressure to the cell
choices.explanation: A cell wall does not move ions across the membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lipid bilayer only, because the ions dissolve in the hydrophobic interior and move through it using the energy of the ions
choices.explanation: Ions do not dissolve in the hydrophobic interior, and active transport needs energy and proteins.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metabolic energy, such as ATP, and a membrane protein that carries out the transport
choices.explanation: Active transport requires metabolic energy and membrane proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A concentration gradient only, because the ions move across the membrane because of their concentration difference
choices.explanation: Movement driven only by a concentration gradient is passive transport.

explanation: Active transport requires metabolic energy and membrane proteins.

stem: Which statement best describes the function of the sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase) in an animal cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It uses energy from ATP to move sodium ions and potassium ions across the membrane against their gradients, which helps maintain the membrane potential.
choices.explanation: The pump is a membrane protein that uses ATP for active transport, and it contributes to the membrane potential.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It allows sodium ions and potassium ions to move down their concentration gradients without using energy, which uses up the membrane potential.
choices.explanation: This describes channel proteins, not the pump, and the pump helps to maintain the membrane potential.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It uses energy from ATP to move water across the membrane against its concentration gradient, which maintains the volume of the cell.
choices.explanation: The pump moves ions. Water moves by osmosis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes ATP by letting sodium ions and potassium ions move through the membrane, which provides energy for other cell processes.
choices.explanation: The pump uses ATP. It does not make it.

explanation: The Na⁺/K⁺ pump is an ATPase that carries out active transport and maintains the membrane potential.

stem: A poison stops a nerve cell from making ATP. Which prediction about the concentrations of sodium ions and potassium ions across its membrane is most consistent with what is known about active transport?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The concentration gradients of the ions will not change, because ions cannot cross the membrane without the action of a pump.
choices.explanation: Ions leak across the membrane through channels, so the gradients decrease without pumping.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The concentration gradients of the ions will reverse at once, because the poison turns the pumps into channel proteins.
choices.explanation: The poison stops the production of ATP. It does not change the proteins into channels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The concentration gradients of the ions will increase, because the pumps continue to move ions after the ATP has been used up in the cell.
choices.explanation: The pumps need ATP, so they stop working without it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The concentration gradients of the ions will gradually decrease, because ions move down their gradients through channels and the pumps no longer work.
choices.explanation: Active transport maintains the gradients. Without ATP the pumps stop, and ions move down their gradients.

explanation: Active transport requires energy to maintain gradients, so the gradients dissipate when ATP production stops.

stem: Cells were placed in a solution that contained 0.10 mM of a molecule, and the concentration of the molecule inside the cells was measured after 30 minutes, with and without a chemical that stops the production of ATP, as shown in the table. Which conclusion is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The molecule is probably taken into the cells by facilitated diffusion, because the chemical had no effect on the uptake.
choices.explanation: The chemical greatly reduced the uptake, so energy was needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The molecule is probably taken into the cells by simple diffusion, because the concentration inside the cells became higher than outside.
choices.explanation: Simple diffusion would move the molecule down its gradient, so it could not raise the concentration inside above the outside concentration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The molecule is probably taken into the cells by active transport, because uptake against the concentration gradient required ATP.
choices.explanation: Without the inhibitor the cells accumulated the molecule to a concentration inside that was about 50 times the concentration outside. This did not occur when ATP production was stopped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The molecule is probably not taken into the cells, because the concentration inside was 0.1 mM when ATP production was stopped.
choices.explanation: The concentration inside was 5.2 mM when ATP was available, so the molecule is taken in.

explanation: Uptake against a gradient that depends on ATP indicates active transport.

rows: With a chemical that stops ATP production
diagram.caption: Uptake of a molecule by cells

stem: Why must a cell continuously use energy to maintain a sodium ion concentration gradient across its plasma membrane?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sodium ions become denatured over time, so the pumps must keep replacing the old sodium ions with new ones.
choices.explanation: Ions are not denatured. They move across the membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sodium ions are made inside the cell by the pumps, so the pumps must keep supplying the cell with new sodium ions all the time.
choices.explanation: The pumps move ions that already exist and do not make them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sodium ions leak back across the membrane through channels, down their gradient, so the pumps must keep moving them out.
choices.explanation: Ions tend to move down their gradients, so gradients and the electrochemical gradient need constant active transport to be maintained.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sodium ions are not able to cross the membrane in either direction, so the gradient would stay the same without energy.
choices.explanation: Ions can cross the membrane through channels, which is why the gradient decays without pumping.

explanation: Metabolic energy is needed to establish and maintain electrochemical gradients.

stem: A researcher studies a membrane protein that moves a substance across the membrane. Which observation would best indicate that the protein is an ATP-powered pump rather than a channel?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The substance moves down its concentration gradient, and the movement continues at the same rate when the supply of ATP is removed.
choices.explanation: This is what is expected for a channel or a transport protein for passive transport.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The substance moves more quickly when the temperature is lowered, and the movement stops when the membrane is made thinner.
choices.explanation: Neither observation shows that the protein uses ATP to move the substance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The substance moves in both directions at the same rate, and the movement does not depend on the concentration on either side.
choices.explanation: This does not show that the protein uses ATP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The substance moves against its concentration gradient, and the movement stops when the supply of ATP is removed.
choices.explanation: A pump uses ATP to move a substance against its gradient. A channel allows only movement down the gradient.

explanation: Active transport needs ATP and can move a substance against its gradient.

stem: Which statement best describes how membranes and membrane-bound organelles compartmentalize a eukaryotic cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They combine all of the metabolic processes of the cell into a single region, so that every enzyme can reach every substrate in the cell.
choices.explanation: Compartmentalization separates processes. It does not combine them into one region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They store the genetic information of the cell in each organelle, so that every compartment can make its own proteins.
choices.explanation: Compartmentalization is about separating reactions and processes. DNA is not stored in every organelle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They prevent any molecules from moving between regions of the cell, so each organelle must make everything that it needs.
choices.explanation: Molecules are moved between compartments, for example in vesicles and through membrane proteins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They separate metabolic processes and specific enzymatic reactions into different regions of the cell, so each takes place in its own environment.
choices.explanation: Compartmentalization keeps different reactions in separate regions of the cell.

explanation: Membranes compartmentalize intracellular metabolic processes and specific enzymatic reactions.

stem: Lysosomes keep their hydrolytic enzymes inside a membrane. Which statement best explains why this is important to the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The membrane separates the enzymes from the cytoplasm, which minimizes competing interactions and keeps them from digesting the cell's own components.
choices.explanation: Internal membranes minimize competing interactions by keeping some reactions away from other parts of the cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The membrane gives the enzymes their energy, because ATP is stored in the membrane of the lysosome until the enzymes need it.
choices.explanation: Membranes do not supply energy to enzymes in this way.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The membrane makes the lysosomes larger, which increases the surface area of the cell and so allows it to exchange more materials.
choices.explanation: The lysosome membrane does not increase the surface area of the plasma membrane of the cell.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The membrane makes the enzymes work more quickly, because the enzymes can digest material only when they are surrounded by a membrane first.
choices.explanation: Enclosure is not what speeds up the enzymes. It separates their activity from the cytoplasm.

explanation: Internal membranes minimize competing interactions and protect the rest of the cell from enzymes.

stem: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion has many folds. Which statement best explains how this feature contributes to the compartmentalization of reactions in the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The folds separate the organelle from the cytoplasm, so no molecules can move into or out of the mitochondrion.
choices.explanation: The outer membrane and the folds do not stop all movement of molecules across the membranes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The folds increase the surface area of membrane on which the reactions of the electron transport chain can take place.
choices.explanation: Internal membranes increase the surface area where reactions can occur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The folds make a second nucleus inside the organelle, which controls the reactions that take place within the mitochondrion.
choices.explanation: Mitochondria do not contain a second nucleus. The folds are part of the inner membrane.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The folds decrease the surface area of the membrane, so the reactions are concentrated into a very small part of the organelle.
choices.explanation: Folds increase the surface area and do not decrease it.

explanation: Internal membranes increase the surface area where reactions can occur.

stem: A drug damages the membranes of lysosomes so that they leak. Which prediction is most consistent with the role of lysosomes and of compartmentalization?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cell would produce more ATP than before, because the lysosome enzymes would supply energy to the mitochondria of the cell.
choices.explanation: Hydrolytic enzymes break down molecules and do not supply ATP to the mitochondria.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hydrolytic enzymes would escape into the cytoplasm and could digest components of the cell, which could lead to cell death.
choices.explanation: Without the membrane, the enzymes are no longer separated from the rest of the cell, and lysosomes also play a role in cell death.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cell would make more proteins than before, because the enzymes that escape from the lysosomes would increase protein synthesis.
choices.explanation: The enzymes are hydrolytic, so they break molecules down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cell would not be affected, because the enzymes work only inside the lysosome and are inactive anywhere else in the cell.
choices.explanation: The enzymes would be able to act on components in the cytoplasm if they escape.

explanation: Compartmentalization protects the cell from its own digestive enzymes.

stem: Which choice lists only membrane-bound structures of a eukaryotic cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes and vacuoles
choices.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex and lysosomes
choices.explanation: All of these are surrounded by membranes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The nucleus, the cytoskeleton, the Golgi complex, lysosomes and ribosomes
choices.explanation: The cytoskeleton and ribosomes have no membrane.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondria, ribosomes, the Golgi complex, vacuoles and the cell wall
choices.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane, and the cell wall is not a membrane-bound structure.

explanation: The nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi complex and lysosomes are membrane-bound.

stem: A eukaryotic cell builds fatty acids in one compartment and breaks fatty acids down in another compartment. Which statement best explains the advantage of this arrangement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The two pathways are always active at the same time in the same place, which makes the cell produce more energy at the same time.
choices.explanation: Separating the pathways keeps them from running together in the same place.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The enzymes of the two pathways move between the compartments, which lets each enzyme catalyze the reaction of the other pathway.
choices.explanation: Enzymes are specific to their reactions and are kept in their own compartments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The enzymes of the two opposing pathways are kept apart, so the pathways do not interfere and can be regulated separately.
choices.explanation: Internal membranes minimize competing interactions between processes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The membranes between the compartments provide the energy for both pathways, so that the cell does not have to make ATP.
choices.explanation: Membranes do not provide energy for the pathways.

explanation: Compartmentalization minimizes competing interactions between processes.

stem: According to the theory of endosymbiosis, from what did mitochondria and chloroplasts evolve?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Free-living prokaryotic cells that were taken in by an ancestor of eukaryotic cells and became organelles inside it
choices.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts evolved from once free-living prokaryotes by endosymbiosis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pieces of the nucleus that grew their own membranes and moved into the cytoplasm of the ancestral eukaryotic cell long ago
choices.explanation: The theory states that they came from free-living prokaryotes, not from the nucleus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vesicles of the endomembrane system that gained DNA from the nucleus and then took over the production of ATP
choices.explanation: The theory involves once free-living prokaryotes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Viruses that infected the ancestral eukaryotic cell and replaced its metabolic enzymes with enzymes that make ATP
choices.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are thought to have come from prokaryotic cells and not from viruses.

explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts evolved from free-living prokaryotes by endosymbiosis.

stem: Which observation provides the best support for the claim that mitochondria evolved from free-living bacteria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mitochondria are the largest organelles in most cells, and they are easier to see than other organelles with a light microscope.
choices.explanation: The size of an organelle says nothing about its origin.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mitochondria use oxygen in cellular respiration, and the oxygen they use is released by the chloroplasts in plant cells.
choices.explanation: The use of oxygen does not show that mitochondria evolved from bacteria.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria are found in the cells of animals, plants and fungi, and they are the site of the production of most of the cell's ATP.
choices.explanation: Being found in many organisms does not show that they came from bacteria.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA and ribosomes like those of bacteria, and they are surrounded by a double membrane.
choices.explanation: These features of mitochondria are similar to those of prokaryotes, which supports an ancestral relationship.

explanation: Features shared with bacteria support the claim that mitochondria evolved from free-living bacteria.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the compartmentalization of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prokaryotic cells have no specialized structures of any kind inside, and eukaryotic cells have only one internal membrane around the DNA.
choices.explanation: Prokaryotes have internal regions with specialized structures, and eukaryotic cells have many internal membranes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prokaryotic cells typically lack internal membrane-bound organelles, whereas eukaryotic cells have internal membranes that partition the cell.
choices.explanation: Prokaryotes have specialized regions without membrane-bound organelles, and eukaryotes have internal membranes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prokaryotic cells and eukaryotic cells both have a nucleus, mitochondria and an endomembrane system that divide the cell into parts.
choices.explanation: Prokaryotes typically lack these membrane-bound organelles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prokaryotic cells have more internal membrane-bound organelles than eukaryotic cells have, and eukaryotic cells have no specialized regions of any kind.
choices.explanation: This reverses the comparison. Eukaryotic cells have internal membranes.

explanation: Eukaryotic cells have internal membranes that partition the cell; prokaryotes typically do not have membrane-bound organelles.

stem: A newly discovered single-celled organism has a plasma membrane, a cell wall, ribosomes and DNA, but no nucleus and no mitochondria. Which statement about the organism is best supported by what is known about cell structure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a eukaryote, because it has a cell wall, which is a membrane-bound organelle that is found only in eukaryotes.
choices.explanation: A cell wall is not a membrane-bound organelle, and prokaryotes also have cell walls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot be a living cell, because every living cell must have a nucleus that contains its genetic information.
choices.explanation: Prokaryotic cells are alive and do not have a nucleus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a eukaryote, because it has ribosomes and DNA, which are found only in cells that have a nucleus and mitochondria.
choices.explanation: Ribosomes and DNA are found in all forms of life, including prokaryotes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a prokaryote, because it typically lacks internal membrane-bound organelles, although it may have specialized regions.
choices.explanation: The absence of membrane-bound organelles such as a nucleus and mitochondria is typical of a prokaryotic cell.

explanation: Prokaryotes typically lack internal membrane-bound organelles.

stem: The table compares features of mitochondria, bacteria and the nuclear genome of a eukaryotic cell. Which claim is best supported by the data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mitochondria share several features with the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell that they do not share with bacteria, which shows that they evolved from the nucleus of the cell.
choices.explanation: The table shows that mitochondria match bacteria in each feature.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacteria and the eukaryotic nucleus are the same in all of the features shown in the table, so they must have a common origin.
choices.explanation: The table shows that bacteria and the nucleus differ in each feature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondria are different from bacteria in all of the features shown in the table, which shows that they cannot be related to them.
choices.explanation: The table shows that mitochondria are similar to bacteria in every feature listed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondria share several features with bacteria that they do not share with the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell, supporting the claim that mitochondria evolved from bacteria.
choices.explanation: The shape of the DNA, the type of division and the type of ribosomes all match those of bacteria.

explanation: Shared features support an evolutionary relationship.
